const body = `IDEA: CURVALLOC-LORENTZ-RQ
TITLE: Mean-zero allocation of per-level Lorentz curvature and code radius from the null-standardised Ollivier curvature of the training behaviour quotient graph.
MOTIVATION: The measured evidence says the recall-relevant geometric object is the *profile across RQ levels* of the behaviour quotient graph's standardised Ollivier curvature (L3 +0.26, L1 -0.16, L1-L3 -0.20, p=0.0095), and that the largest non-geometric driver is how many level-3 codes actually get used (+0.42, with collisions -0.39). Existing SIDs therefore differ in whether their prefix geometry happens to fit the behaviour graph's level-wise clustering. The problem is that no quantizer currently *builds* that fit: the partition is produced by a Euclidean nearest-code rule under one curvature for all levels.
NOVELTY: Not a per-level learning rate from a hard prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), not entropy-ranked radial assignment (BRad-RQ), not Frechet codebook updates, and not a fixed mixed-curvature product. The signal is a runtime-measured, permutation-null-standardised Ollivier curvature of the *behaviour quotient graph induced by the current prefix assignment*, and it is spent as a mean-zero allocation of two geometric quantities (per-level negative curvature c_l and per-level radial budget rho_l) that enter the distance the quantizer itself minimises. No extra loss term is added, no recall label is used, and the assignment feeds back into the measurement, so behaviour and geometry form a closed loop rather than two parallel objectives.
CHANGE: Each RQ level l lives on its own Lorentz hyperboloid of curvature -c_l, and its code radius is rho_l; both are set from the level's standardised behaviour-quotient curvature, c_l = c0*exp(-delta_l) and rho_l = rho0*exp(delta_l/2) with delta_l = kappa_hat_l - mean_l(kappa_hat_l). Nearest-code assignment, residual subtraction and codebook parameterisation all happen through the exp/log maps of that level's hyperboloid, so changing delta_l changes which code each item gets.
SPECIFICATION: (1) Build the training co-occurrence graph W once: W_ij = number of training-split sessions where j occurs after i within the same window H used by the sequential Stage-2 encoder, symmetrised W <- (W+W^T)/2; N_tr = 24556. (2) Every T = 200 epochs (15 refreshes in the 3000-epoch budget) take the current hard prefixes p_l(i) = (k_1..k_l) and form the quotient graph Q_l: nodes = occupied level-l prefixes, A_l(a,b) = sum_{i in a, j in b} W_ij (sparse S_l^T W S_l, self-loops kept); d_Q = unweighted hop distance. (3) Lazy walk P = 0.5(I + D^{-1}A), curvature kappa(a,b) = 1 - W1(m_a,m_b)/d_Q(a,b) with m_a = 0.5 delta_a + 0.5 A_a./deg(a). (4) Standardise against a member-shuffling null: R = 8 relabellings of items into prefixes with the group sizes preserved; kappa_hat_l = (kappa_bar_l - mu_null,l)/sigma_null,l. (5) Set delta_l as above with the mean-zero constraint, clip delta_l to [-1,+1], EMA with 0.5. (6) All distances, residuals and codebooks use the level's own hyperboloid. STOP-GRADIENT on kappa_hat (it is a schedule, not a loss).
COST: Per step the extra work is three Lorentz distance tensors of shape B x K x (D+1) plus three exp/log maps of shape B x D per item and per code: about 1.2e6 extra flops at B=256, K=256, D=64, i.e. under 2% of a step, no extra backward pass through the measurement. The 15 curvature refreshes cost one sparse S_l^T W S_l per level (3 x nnz(W) ~ 3e6 adds), 8 null relabellings and 3 x 256 sampled edges x 30 Sinkhorn iterations on supports of at most 9+9 cells (~1.5e7 flops per refresh, a few seconds each), so roughly 30-60 s of the whole 3000 x 24 = 72000-step run: under 1% wall clock, no extra memory beyond one 24556 x 3 assignment cache.
HYPOTHESIS: If the level-wise clustering of the training behaviour graph is a real constraint on a good prefix code, then letting the sub-quotient that is more clustered (typically level 3) own a flatter, wider hyperboloid while the more branching level (typically level 1) owns a sharper, tighter one must (a) leave level-3 code usage at or above baseline, (b) not collapse level-1 usage, (c) make the run's measured standardised profile monotone in depth, and (d) push Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065. Observed from the run's own logs: per-level used-code counts, the 15 recorded kappa_hat triples, and test_recall@10 against the 0.065 target; if the profile is not monotone or level-1 usage drops below ~8 codes, the hypothesis is falsified.
RISKS: The sign of the curvature-to-geometry map may be wrong for this data (flatter should perhaps follow *low* curvature), which one run cannot correct; mitigated by clipping delta to +-1 so the worst case is a bounded factor-e perturbation of one level rather than a collapse. The assignment<->curvature loop can oscillate; mitigated by T=200 cadence, EMA 0.5 and the mean-zero constraint. Sinkhorn W1 on sparse quotient graphs is noisy and biased upward; the same estimator is applied to the null, so the standardisation cancels the bias but amplifies variance when sigma_null is small. The tangent-space residual chain is less faithful than the Euclidean one, so reconstruction can degrade; mitigated by the measured radial normalisation that makes the tanh squash near-identity for typical items.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Sequential co-consumption / directed item transitions of the training split, aggregated to prefix-group level (the quotient graph), plus the current model's training-item prefix assignment.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only: for every consecutive pair (i -> j) in a training session within window H, increment W_ij; symmetrise. At each refresh, multiply by the current item->prefix indicator per level to get A_l, then the lazy random walk and the per-edge Ollivier curvature with a Sinkhorn-W1 on each sampled edge's neighbour support. Nothing about users, items or interactions from validation or test enters.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: W, the quotient graphs, the null draws and the sigma estimates are computed exclusively from training-split sessions of the frozen Stage-2 split; validation and test interactions are never read during SID construction, and the mechanism contains no validation-based selection, no early stopping and no test-time statistic. The 0.065 target and the forensic correlations are used only to choose the mechanism's direction before the run, never inside the computation; no recall label of any model enters kappa_hat.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Trainable-free but measured negative curvature per level, c_l = c0*exp(-delta_l) with c0 = 1, realised by the Lorentz hyperboloid model of curvature -c_l: d_{L,c}(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c))*arcosh(-c<x,y>_L), exp_o^c(v) = (cosh(sqrt(c)||v||)/sqrt(c), sinh(sqrt(c)||v||)/(sqrt(c)||v||) * v), log_o^c its inverse; the Euclidean branch is the c->0 limit.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer: the codebook parameterisation (each code is exp_o^{c_l} of a squashed free tangent vector at radius rho_l), the encoder-side residual mapping exp_o^{c_l}, the nearest-code rule (argmin of d_{L,c_l}) and the residual subtraction in the tangent space log_o^{c_l}. It therefore acts on assignment and on every gradient that reaches the encoder and codebooks.
COUPLING PATH: training behaviour graph W -> quotient graph Q_l of the current prefixes -> standardised Ollivier curvature kappa_hat_l -> delta_l -> (c_l, rho_l) -> Lorentz distance d_{L,c_l}(exp_o^{c_l}(rho_l-squash(r_l,i)), e_{l,k}) -> argmin / straight-through -> new prefixes -> next refresh of Q_l. Removing the behaviour term collapses kappa_hat to 0 and sets every level to unit curvature and the median radius; removing the curved geometry (c_l -> 0 with rho_l kept) leaves a Euclidean quantizer with the same behaviour-driven radius. Both change the argmin, hence the SID.
COUPLING EQUATION: p_l(k|i) = softmax_k( -d_{L,c_l}( exp_o^{c_l}( rho_l*tanh(||r_{l,i}||/rho_l)*rhat_{l,i} ), exp_o^{c_l}( rho_l*tanh(||w_{l,k}||/rho_l)*what_{l,k} ) ) ), with c_l = c0*exp(-delta_l), rho_l = rho0*exp(delta_l/2), delta_l = clip( kappa_hat_l - mean_m kappa_hat_m , -1, +1 ), kappa_hat_l = (kappa_bar_l(A_l(W_train, p_l)) - mu_null,l)/sigma_null,l, and rho0 = median_i ||z_i - mean(z)|| measured on training items at epoch 0.
OBSERVABLES: per-level used-code counts over training (especially level 3, expected at or above baseline, and level 1, expected not to collapse); the 15 logged kappa_hat triples and their depth profile; collision rate of the final SID table; the recorded behaviour-prefix transfer predictability (diagnostic only, never a gate); final Stage3 test_recall@10 against 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: delta_l = 0 for all levels, i.e. W is not read, c_l = c0 and rho_l = rho0; everything else identical (still Lorentzian, unit curvature, median radius).
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c_l replaced by the flat limit c -> 0 (Euclidean squared distance, no arcosh, no exp/log) while delta_l and rho_l keep their behaviour-driven values, i.e. a Euclidean quantizer with behaviour-set radius.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full loop above, kappa_hat measured from the training quotient graph and spent on both c_l and rho_l. Only this arm is trained in this round; the other two exist in code behind switches and are correct but are not run.
SPEC EQUATIONS: see the pseudocode below.
  # once, from training split only
  W = sym(cooccurrence(train_sessions, window=H)); N = 24556
  rho0 = median_i ||z_i - mean(z)||            # measured at epoch 0
  c0 = 1.0; delta = zeros(3)
  for epoch in 1..3000:
      for step in 1..24:
          for l in 1..3:
              c_l = c0*exp(-delta[l]); rho_l = rho0*exp(delta[l]/2)
              v = rho_l * tanh(||r_l||/rho_l) * rhat_l          # squash residual
              x = exp_o(c_l, v)                                 # item side
              E = exp_o(c_l, rho_l*tanh(||w_l||/rho_l)*what_l)  # codes, free params w_l
              logits = -d_L(c_l, x[:,None,:], E[None,:,:])
              k_l = argmin(logits, dim=-1)                      # ST estimator
              u_l = log_o(c_l, E[k_l])                          # tangent code
              r_{l+1} = r_l - u_l
          z_hat = LayerNorm(sum_l u_l); loss = recon + commit + baseline usage term
          backward/Adam on encoder and w_l                     # c_l, rho_l are stop-grad
      if epoch % 200 == 0:
          for l in 1..3:
              A_l = S_l(p_l)^T @ W @ S_l(p_l)                   # quotient graph
              d_Q = hopdist(A_l); P = 0.5*(I + D^{-1}A_l)
              kappa_bar_l = mean over 256 weight-sampled edges of (1 - sinkhorn_W1(m_a,m_b,d_Q)/d_Q(a,b))
              for r in 1..8:  p_l^null = shuffle_members(p_l) (sizes preserved)
                             recompute kappa_bar_l^null the same way
              mu,sigma = mean,std(kappa_bar_l^null)
              kappa_hat_l = (kappa_bar_l - mu)/max(sigma, 1e-6)
          delta = 0.5*delta + 0.5*clip(kappa_hat - mean(kappa_hat), -1, +1)
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: training-split co-occurrence W, item representations z_i and residuals r_{l,i}, current hard prefixes, free codebook tangents w_{l,k}, measured rho0. Outputs: per-level (c_l, rho_l) refresh every 200 epochs, per-item codes k_1..k_3 (the SID), the tangent code vectors u_l for the decoder, and the decoded reconstruction used by the standard RQ-VAE loss.
SAFEGUARDS: arcosh argument clamped to >= 1+1e-7 and only evaluated in float32 after subtracting the time component, with the c<=1e-4 branch replaced by the Euclidean formula; every code and residual is squashed by rho_l*tanh(.) so sqrt(c_l)||v|| <= sqrt(c_l)*rho_l stays O(1) and exp_o cannot overflow; delta clipped to +-1 (one standardised sigma -> factor e) and EMA-smoothed 0.5 so a noisy null cannot jump the geometry; kappa_hat set to 0 whenever a level has fewer than 8 occupied prefixes or sigma_null < 1e-6 (graceful fallback to unit curvature, which is also the behaviour-off arm); mean-zero constraint on delta so total curvature budget is conserved and code usage cannot be globally inflated or deflated; rho0 measured from training items so the squash is near-identity for typical residuals; the standard usage/entropy term and the codebook size are untouched, so nothing forces prefix merging and the Issue #127 coarse-partition collapse cannot be reproduced by construction.
END IDEA`;
await tools.progress.append_progress({content: body});
return "ok";

COUPLING EQUATION: p_l(k|i) = softmax_k( -d_{L,c_l}( exp_o^{c_l}( rho_l*tanh(||r_{l,i}||/rho_l)*rhat_{l,i} ), exp_o^{c_l}( rho_l*tanh(||w_{l,k}||/rho_l)*what_{l,k} ) ) ), with c_l = c0*exp(-delta_l), rho_l = rho0*exp(delta_l/2), delta_l = clip(kappa_hat_l - mean_m kappa_hat_m, -1, +1), kappa_hat_l = (kappa_bar_l(A_l(W_train, p_l)) - mu_null,l)/sigma_null,l, and rho0 = median_i ||z_i - mean(z)|| measured on training items at epoch 0.
OBSERVABLES: per-level used-code counts over training (level 3 expected at or above baseline, level 1 expected not to collapse); the 15 logged kappa_hat triples and their depth profile; the final SID table's collision rate; the recorded behaviour-prefix transfer predictability (diagnostic only, never a gate); final Stage3 test_recall@10 against 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: delta_l = 0 for all levels, i.e. W is not read, c_l = c0 and rho_l = rho0; everything else identical (still Lorentzian, unit curvature, median radius).
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c_l replaced by the flat limit c -> 0 (Euclidean squared distance, no arcosh, no exp/log) while delta_l and rho_l keep their behaviour-driven values, i.e. a Euclidean quantizer with behaviour-set radius.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full loop above, kappa_hat measured from the training quotient graph and spent on both c_l and rho_l. Only this arm is trained this round; the other two exist behind switches, are correct, and are not run.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
  # once, from the training split only
  W = sym(cooccurrence(train_sessions, window=H)); N = 24556
  rho0 = median_i ||z_i - mean(z)||          # measured at epoch 0
  c0 = 1.0; delta = zeros(3)
  for epoch in 1..3000:
      for step in 1..24:
          for l in 1..3:
              c_l = c0*exp(-delta[l]); rho_l = rho0*exp(delta[l]/2)
              x   = exp_o(c_l, rho_l*tanh(||r_l||/rho_l)*rhat_l)          # item side
              E   = exp_o(c_l, rho_l*tanh(||w_l||/rho_l)*what_l)          # codes, free tangents w_l
              logits = -d_L(c_l, x[:,None,:], E[None,:,:])
              k_l = argmin(logits, -1)                                    # straight-through
              u_l = log_o(c_l, E[k_l])                                    # tangent code
              r_{l+1} = r_l - u_l
          z_hat = LayerNorm(sum_l u_l); loss = recon + commit + baseline usage term
          adam_step(encoder, {w_l})                                       # c_l, rho_l stop-grad
      if epoch % 200 == 0:
          for l in 1..3:
              A_l = S_l(p_l)^T @ W @ S_l(p_l)                              # quotient graph
              d_Q = hopdist(A_l); P = 0.5*(I + D^{-1}A_l)
              kappa_bar_l = mean over 256 weight-sampled edges of (1 - sinkhornW1(m_a,m_b,d_Q)/d_Q(a,b))
              for r in 1..8:
                  p_l^null = shuffle_members(p_l)                          # group sizes preserved
                  recompute kappa_bar_l^null identically
              mu, sigma = mean/std(kappa_bar_l^null)
              kappa_hat_l = (kappa_bar_l - mu)/max(sigma, 1e-6)
          delta = 0.5*delta + 0.5*clip(kappa_hat - mean(kappa_hat), -1, +1)
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: training-split co-occurrence W, item representations z_i and residuals r_{l,i}, current hard prefixes, free codebook tangents w_{l,k}, measured rho0. Outputs: per-level (c_l, rho_l) refreshed every 200 epochs, per-item codes k_1..k_3 (the SID), the tangent code vectors u_l for the decoder, and the reconstruction consumed by the standard RQ-VAE loss.
SAFEGUARDS: arcosh argument clamped to >= 1+1e-7, evaluated in float32 after subtracting the time component, with the c <= 1e-4 branch replaced by the Euclidean formula; every code and residual squashed by rho_l*tanh(.) so sqrt(c_l)||v|| <= sqrt(c_l)*rho_l stays O(1) and exp_o cannot overflow; delta clipped to +-1 (one standardised sigma maps to a factor e) and EMA-smoothed 0.5 so a noisy null cannot jump the geometry; kappa_hat set to 0 whenever a level has fewer than 8 occupied prefixes or sigma_null < 1e-6, which falls back to unit curvature (also the behaviour-off arm); mean-zero constraint on delta so the total curvature budget is conserved and code usage cannot be globally inflated or deflated; rho0 measured from training items so the squash is near-identity for typical residuals; the standard usage/entropy term and the codebook size are untouched, so nothing forces prefix merging and the Issue #127 coarse-partition collapse cannot be reproduced by construction.
END IDEA
